## Key Insights

1. Kharif Sowing Status: Kharif sowing data collection has started from 06 th  June, 2025 and the sowing is in  preliminary  stage.  As  on  13 th   June,  2025,  the  area  sown  under  Kharif  crops  is 89.29 lakh ha (including 55.07 lakh ha (105% of normal area) in Sugarcane) as compared to 87.81 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. (The normal area coverage during Kharif is estimated to be more than 1100 lakh ha.)

## 2. Weather Update:

- a) Temperature: Maximum Temperatures likely to fall by 3-5°C over Northwest India during next  24  hours  and  no  significant  change  thereafter.  No  significant  change  in  maximum temperatures  likely  over  Central  India  during  next  24  hours  and  gradual  fall  by  2-4°C thereafter during subsequent 5 days. Maximum Temperatures likely to fall by 3-4°C over Northwest India during next 3 days and no significant change thereafter. No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country.
- b) Rainfall Distribution: From June 01- 15 June, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 31% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: (-)39%; (ii) Northwest India: (-)38%; (iii) Central India: (-)34%; and South Peninsula: (-) 11%.
3.  Extremely heavy rainfall likely at isolated places over Coastal Karnataka, Konkan & Goa during 16 th  & 17 th  June.
4.  Fairly  widespread  to  widespread  rainfall  activity  likely  over  West,  Northwest,  East, Northeast India, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Costal Karnataka, North Costal Andhra Pradesh and Lakshadweep; Isolated to scattered rainfall likely over Remaining parts of the country .
5.  Light/moderate rainfall  at  some/isolated  places  accompanied  with  accompanied  with thunderstorm, lightning & gusty winds likely over most parts of the country.
6.  Rainfall  is  likely  to  be  below  normal  in  Northwest India  and  NE  India. Above  normal rainfall activity is likely over Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, East M.P., Maharashtra and Odisha.
7.  Monsoon likely to be in active phase with heavy to very heavy rainfall at a few places and extremely heavy falls (>20 cm) at isolated places over south peninsular India and Konkan & Goa till 16th June, 2025.

## 3. Inputs Situation:

- a) Water Reservoir Status : As on 12 th  June 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 55.52 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 30.4% of total live storage capacity (182.44 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 140

The  overall  storage  position  is  better than  the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is  also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.

- b) Groundwater Levels : Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014-2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024.
- c) Seeds  and  Fertilizers :  For  Kharif  2025,  certified  seed  availability  is  178.64  lakh  quintals against a requirement of 164.05 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 14.60 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products.
4. Pests & Diseases: Over all intensity of pests and disease remained below Economic Threshold Level (ETL) and no major pest incidence was recorded.

## Rainfall Forecast:

-  Overall  rainfall  activity  is  likely  to  be  above  most  parts  of  the  country  except  south Peninsular India; where below normal rainfall activity is likely during the week.

## Advance of Southwest Monsoon:

-  The  Northern  Limit  of  Monsoon  continues  to  pass  through  17.0°N/55°E,  17.5°N/60°E, 18°N/65°E, 18.5°N/70°E, Mumbai, Ahilyanagar, Adilabad, Bhawanipatna, Puri, Sandhead Island, 23.5°N/89.5°E, Balurghat, 30°N/85°E.
-  Conditions are favourable for further advancement of Southwest monsoon over some parts of Gujarat, some more parts of Vidarbha, Chhattisgarh & Odisha during next 24 hours; over some parts of West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar and East Uttar Pradesh during subsequent 3 days .

## Temerature

## Week 1 (13 th  - 19 th   June 2025):

-  No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over Central India during next 24 hours and gradual fall by 2-4°C thereafter during subsequent 5 days.
-  Maximum Temperatures likely to fall by 3-4°C over Northwest India during next 3 days and no significant change thereafter.
-  No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country

## Week 2 ( 20 th  - 26 th   June 2025):

-  Maximum temperatures are likely to decrease over northwest India as compared to week 1. These  are  likely  to  be  below  normal  over  most  parts  of  the  country  outside  parts  of Northwest India (Western Himalayan Region and Rajasthan), where it is likely to be near normal.

## 3. RESERVOIR STORAGE (as on 12 th  June, 2025)

Current live storage in 161 reservoirs was 55.52 BCM (30.4%) of total live capacity of 182.44 BCM.

## 4. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION

## (a) Soil Moisture Observation

-  Soil moisture during 07 June - 13 June 2025 was better than the average of the past 9 years in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Western M.P, Maharashtra, Karnataka, A.P., Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal.
-  It was lower than average of past 9 years in Bihar and Eastern UP.

<!-- image -->

## CROP SOWING STATUS FOR KHARIF SEASON

## Kharif Crops - Area coverage

-  Sugarcane: About  55.07  lakh  ha  area  coverage  under  Sugarcane  has  been  reported  as compared to 54.88 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.
-  Cotton: About 13.49 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 13.28 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year
-  Jute :  There  has  been  a  decline  in  area  sown  under  Jute  on  account  of  diversion  towards Maize and Sesamum.

Key Insights

1. Kharif Sowing Status: Kharif sowing data collection has started from 06 th  June, 2025 and the sowing is in  preliminary  stage.  As  on  13 th   June,  2025,  the  area  sown  under  Kharif  crops  is 89.29 lakh ha (including 55.07 lakh ha (105% of normal area) in Sugarcane) as compared to 87.81 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. (The normal area coverage during Kharif is estimated to be more than 1100 lakh ha.)

2. Weather Update:

- a) Temperature: Maximum Temperatures likely to fall by 3-5°C over Northwest India during next  24  hours  and  no  significant  change  thereafter.  No  significant  change  in  maximum temperatures  likely  over  Central  India  during  next  24  hours  and  gradual  fall  by  2-4°C thereafter during subsequent 5 days. Maximum Temperatures likely to fall by 3-4°C over Northwest India during next 3 days and no significant change thereafter. No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country.
- b) Rainfall Distribution: From June 01- 15 June, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 31% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: (-)39%; (ii) Northwest India: (-)38%; (iii) Central India: (-)34%; and South Peninsula: (-) 11%.
3.  Extremely heavy rainfall likely at isolated places over Coastal Karnataka, Konkan & Goa during 16 th  & 17 th  June.
4.  Fairly  widespread  to  widespread  rainfall  activity  likely  over  West,  Northwest,  East, Northeast India, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Costal Karnataka, North Costal Andhra Pradesh and Lakshadweep; Isolated to scattered rainfall likely over Remaining parts of the country .
5.  Light/moderate rainfall  at  some/isolated  places  accompanied  with  accompanied  with thunderstorm, lightning & gusty winds likely over most parts of the country.
6.  Rainfall  is  likely  to  be  below  normal  in  Northwest India  and  NE  India. Above  normal rainfall activity is likely over Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, East M.P., Maharashtra and Odisha.
7.  Monsoon likely to be in active phase with heavy to very heavy rainfall at a few places and extremely heavy falls (>20 cm) at isolated places over south peninsular India and Konkan & Goa till 16th June, 2025.

3. Inputs Situation:

- a) Water Reservoir Status : As on 12 th  June 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 55.52 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 30.4% of total live storage capacity (182.44 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 140

Temerature

Week 1 (13 th  - 19 th   June 2025):

-  No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over Central India during next 24 hours and gradual fall by 2-4°C thereafter during subsequent 5 days.
-  Maximum Temperatures likely to fall by 3-4°C over Northwest India during next 3 days and no significant change thereafter.
